title: Cold rebuild: k-means from start to finish
summary: Rebuild k-means from start to finish from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **k-means from start to finish** in *k-means clustering, and what comes next*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.explain: One row per point, one column per centre. (5, 6) is a little closer to (10, 10): squared distance 41 versus 61.

steps.title: Rebuild k-means from start to finish cold
prompt: Write `kmeans(X, init, iters=50)` that starts from the centres `init` (a `(k, features)` array) and alternates assign and update until the labels stop changing (or `iters` rounds). Return `(labels, centres)`.
Then write `inertia(X, labels, centres)`: the total squared distance from each point to its own centre, a plain float rounded to 2. Lower is tighter.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
